# Team memory

<!-- Generated by Mnemolith from .mnemolith/team/memories/. Don't edit this file: edit the memory's own file, then run `mnemolith team sync`. -->

What this team wants every AI coding tool to know about this project. One line per memory; the full files are in `.mnemolith/team/memories/`.

- Decision: embedding similarity can't tell duplicates from contradictions (in calibration "timeout is 30s" vs "60s" scored 0.94, "we use Postgres" vs "we migrated to MySQL" 0.30). So the engine auto-merges only near-identical text (similarity >= 0.97). For everything else, similar memories are shown to the AI to judge. Don't lower the auto-merge threshold. (decision-embedding-similarity-can-t-tell)
- Decision: staleness compares file contents, not commits. Each linked file is stored as path@<git blob hash> (git hash-object), and recall re-hashes the linked files before every search. That catches uncommitted edits, ignores commits that didn't touch the file, and needs no git hooks. (decision-staleness-compares-file-contents-not)
- Everything runs locally with no telemetry. Data lives under ~/.mnemolith (MNEMOLITH_HOME overrides it): the engine data, its log and pid, the downloaded embedding model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, about 90 MB on first use) and a private Java from Adoptium if none is installed. The first start can take a minute while these download. (everything-runs-locally-with-no-telemetry-data)
- Memories never change silently: every change is a logged event with a timestamp and a reason. The engine writes each memory to the append-only log with the id and timestamp it assigned, so a replay after restart rebuilds the exact same memories and histories. Changes to memory code in Main.java must keep that replay deterministic. (memories-never-change-silently-every-change-is-a)
- mnemolith.md is generated from .mnemolith/team/memories/. Don't edit it by hand: edit the memory's own file, then run `mnemolith team sync`. .gitattributes sets `mnemolith.md merge=union`, so two branches that both add team memories merge without conflicts. Keep that line. (mnemolith-md-is-generated-from-mnemolith-team)
- Mnemolith's engine listens on 127.0.0.1:7380 by default, deliberately not Redis's 6379, so it never collides with a real Redis on the machine. The dashboard (`mnemolith ui`) uses 127.0.0.1:7381. Override them with MNEMOLITH_PORT and MNEMOLITH_UI_PORT. (mnemolith-s-engine-listens-on-127-0-0)
- pom.xml, codecrafters.yml, your_program.sh and .codecrafters/ come from the CodeCrafters "Build Your Own Redis" setup. Don't change the maven-assembly finalName `codecrafters-redis` (the pom says not to), because .codecrafters/run.sh runs /tmp/codecrafters-build-redis-java/codecrafters-redis.jar. These files don't build the Mnemolith package; scripts/build_engine.py does. (pom-xml-codecrafters-yml-your-program-sh-and)
- Releasing: bump the same version in pyproject.toml, mnemolith/__init__.py and server.json (both `version` and `packages[0].version`), commit, then push a tag `vX.Y.Z`. The release workflow fails if any of them disagree with the tag. It publishes to PyPI by trusted publishing and to the MCP Registry by GitHub OIDC, so no tokens are needed. (releasing-bump-the-same-version-in-pyproject-toml)
- Run the tests with `python -m pytest tests`. They don't need the Java engine or the embedding model download: they set config.FAKE_EMBEDDER (env MNEMOLITH_EMBEDDER=fake) and point config.HOME at a tmp folder. Keep new tests the same way, without the engine or the network. (run-the-tests-with-python-m-pytest-tests)
- Team memory code (mnemolith/team.py) writes files under .mnemolith/team/ and mnemolith.md but never runs git commit; people review and commit. It keeps each file's own line endings when rewriting and reads CRLF as LF when fingerprinting, so Windows and Mac agree. A linked folder is fingerprinted file by file, capped at MAX_FOLDER_FILES = 500. (team-memory-code-mnemolith-team-py-writes-files)
- The Claude Code plugin (plugin/) is bumped only after a release is on PyPI: update the version in plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json (the `mnemolith==X` pin in mcpServers too) and plugin/pyproject.toml, run `uv lock` in plugin/, then commit. It can't go first because uv.lock needs the release to exist, and the release workflow runs `uv lock --check` in plugin/. (the-claude-code-plugin-plugin-is-bumped-only)
- The engine jar must stay inside the wheel and sdist: pyproject.toml lists it under hatch `artifacts` because *.jar is gitignored, and the release smoke test fails if the wheel lacks mnemolith/engine/mnemolith-engine.jar. Don't remove those artifacts lines. (the-engine-jar-must-stay-inside-the-wheel)
- The engine records which jar it was started from (sha256 fingerprint in ~/.mnemolith/engine.version). ensure_running restarts it when the installed jar's fingerprint differs, so a rebuilt jar takes effect without stopping the engine by hand. (the-engine-records-which-jar-it-was-started)
- The engine source is src/main/java/Main.java, but the Python package runs the prebuilt jar mnemolith/engine/mnemolith-engine.jar. After changing Main.java, rebuild it with `python scripts/build_engine.py` (needs a JDK) and commit the jar, or the change never reaches users. *.jar is gitignored except this one file. (the-engine-source-is-src-main-java-main)
- The eval (eval/run.py) runs real Claude Code sessions on sample shop codebases in eval/template*/ and needs Claude Code signed in, plus uv, git and make. Use `python3 eval/run.py --dry-run` to check the setup without spending runs. The eval/template*/ folders are test fixtures with deliberate rules, not part of Mnemolith. Results go to eval/runs/, which is gitignored. (the-eval-eval-run-py-runs-real-claude)
- The project used to be called Aether Cache. Backward compatibility is deliberate and must be kept: every MNEMOLITH_* env var also accepts AETHER_* and older MEMORY_* names (config._env), legacy.py moves ~/.aether-cache to ~/.mnemolith once, memory_mcp/server.py keeps old `python memory_mcp/server.py` setups working, and the release still builds the final legacy/aether-cache package. (the-project-used-to-be-called-aether-cache)
- The shipped engine jar is compiled with `javac --release 11`, so it runs on any Java 11+ runtime (engine.py's MIN_JAVA = 11). Main.java must not use language features or APIs newer than Java 11, even though pom.xml and codecrafters.yml target Java 25 with --enable-preview for the CodeCrafters build. (the-shipped-engine-jar-is-compiled-with-javac)
- The website in docs/ is static HTML with shared assets/site.css and assets/site.js, with no build step or framework. Preview it with `python3 -m http.server 4173` from docs/. Absolute share-metadata URLs use https://mnemolith.dev/ (docs/CNAME) and must be updated on every page if the address changes. (the-website-in-docs-is-static-html-with)
